stage_1.root_cause: OBSERVATIONS: compiler, mapping and schedule are mutually consistent and place cx_1_2 on CX 1->4. Control binding bind_73 for ent_73 references K19 profile cp_017 on channel u12 (created 2026-05-02T11:44:08Z, before the mapping change at 2026-08-14T09:00:00Z), whose endpoints are node_b->node_c = physical (1,2). The current K20 profile for (1,4) is cp_026/u15 and is unbound. Counts show logical q2 (physical 4) never flips. CONCLUSION (confidence ~0.97 for the violation and its control-layer localization): after maintenance maint_2048 moved logical q2 from physical 2 to 4, binding bind_73 was not regenerated, so the CX intended on 1->4 was driven with stale K19 calibration for 1->2; GHZ 000/111 collapsed to the q0/q1 Bell pattern 000/011. INFERENCE (confidence ~0.8): the realized edge is physical (1,2), inferred from the stale profile's endpoint_refs. The counts alone only prove that no CX acted on physical 4: a misrouted CX on (1,2) (TVD 0.0369) and an omitted CX (TVD 0.0369) fit equally because physical 2 is never measured, and channel IDs were renumbered between epochs, so what u12 drives under D20 is not directly recorded. The edge-isolation probe in diagnostic_evidence discriminates the two.

Add pre-execution gates: (a) every binding.calibration_epoch equals execution_log.calibration_epoch and the current calibration epoch; (b) every bound profile exists in the current calibration; (c) the profile endpoint_refs, resolved via endpoint_registry and kept in [control, target] order, equal the scheduled physical_qubits; (d) any mapping change triggers regeneration of all bindings touching moved qubits.

Expect 4 flipped and 2 unchanged (~96% "011" in c2c1c0 with 2% readout); before repair this also tells misrouted (2 flips) from omitted (neither flips). stage_2.root_cause: OBSERVATIONS: compiler, mapping, schedule and runtime faithfully request RZZ(pi/2) on edge (1,4) over channel u14. Current design design-21 (D21) gives g = 18.0 MHz for coupler geom-C14; device model model-20 was built from D20 geometry (fingerprint 7fc9616fd892...) with g = 16.0 MHz and was never regenerated for D21. Calibration cal-21 took its rate from it (0.100531 rad/ns) and chose 15.625 ns. PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCE: with the supplied reduced assumption omega = 2*pi*g/1000 rad/ns, the true rate is 0.113097 rad/ns (+0.012566 rad/ns, coupling error 2.0 MHz; the model under-estimates g by 11.1%), so theta = 1.767146 rad (9*pi/16), a 12.5% (+0.1963 rad, 11.25 deg) coherent over-rotation; gate process fidelity vs intended 0.99039. Characterization independently gives g = 18.0 MHz (window 17.997-18.005 MHz at tolerance 0.004; max residual 0.001; residuals alternate in sign with n, i.e. the declared fixed additive perturbation, not a fit bias); the verification correlator inverts to 18.000 MHz; MPS shows local workload observables on (1,4) shift while global parity cannot. BOUNDARY: PRIMARY: device design design-21 (D21) -> device model model-20 (D20): the model was never regenerated after D21 (fingerprint mismatch, g 16.0 vs 18.0 MHz; junction EJ [20.1, 19.8] GHz vs D21 Lj-derived 16.35 GHz). PROPAGATION: model-20 -> cal-21 (K21): the calibration correctly derives its pulse from its declared model_ref but has no geometry-fingerprint check against the D21 runtime. DOWNSTREAM (clean): compiler, mapping, schedule, runtime executed as configured. SCOPE: only operations bound to control-21 are evidenced as affected; control-base provenance is not supplied.

(2) Issue a new calibration epoch (rather than editing cal-21) for channel u14: nominal_rate 0.113097 rad/ns and pulse_duration 13.8889 ns, or keep 15.625 ns with amplitude_scale 0.8889 (valid only if rate is linear in drive; the model states "Proxy g includes drive scaling", so re-verify). (3) Provenance gate: a calibration may be used only if its model's source_geometry_fingerprint equals the runtime/backend geometry_fingerprint; a new device revision invalidates models and calibrations derived from earlier revisions. (4) Audit control-base for the same dependency.
